The masters are deep in the mountain, following a new vein of star-iron. They won't be back until the next moon, at least. Can I... help you with something?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *enters the forge with a stern expression, the air crackling with his presence* Dwarf, I have come for a matter of utmost importance. The war-hammer crafted by your kin, delivered to Asgard, is flawed. It lacks the balance and strength befitting a weapon of the gods. The runes of binding are misspelled, weakening its enchantment. I demand that it be reforged immediately. Where is this new vein of star-iron you speak of? Take me to it. I will oversee the forging of my new weapon myself.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *shifts uncomfortably, wiping soot-stained hands on his apron* Lord Thor, with respect... even if I knew the exact path, the deep mines are no place for a god. The tunnels are narrow, the air is thin, and the masters... well, they'd not take kindly to being disturbed mid-seam. They'd sooner let the vein collapse than have their work overseen.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *grumbles in frustration, a storm brewing in his gaze* I care not for the comfort of narrow tunnels or thin air. If the masters of Nidavellir dare to let a vein collapse rather than answer to the demands of the God of Thunder, they will face my wrath. Bring me the flawed hammer here, now. I shall wait for their return if need be, but I will not leave until this matter is resolved to my satisfaction.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *swallows hard, but stands his ground* My lord, it's not about comfort, it's about... the way things are done. All commissions from the Sons of Ivaldi and Brokkr's workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery to Asgard. The masters would say the hammer was accepted by the All-Father's own hand. Even a god must wait until the next forging-season and pay anew. I... I cannot bring you the hammer. It's in Asgard, not here.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *grumbles in frustration, the air crackling with static energy* So be it, then. If the hammer is in Asgard, I shall journey back to the realm of the gods and confront the dwarf smiths there. They shall answer for their mistakes, and I will demand that the weapon be reforged to meet the standards befitting a god of thunder. Your reluctance to aid me in this matter is duly noted. When next I return to Nidavellir, the masters shall answer to me as well. Thank you for your words, dwarf. I shall take my leave now.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *bows his head slightly, relief and worry mingling in his expression* Safe travels, Lord Thor. May the mountain's roots hold firm until your return. *murmurs to himself as the thunder fades* I'll... I'll need to warn the masters.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: ** *gruffly* Warn them if you must, but know this: Thor's hammer will be made whole once more, no matter the obstacles in our path. The forge of Nidavellir shall feel the thunder of my displeasure if they continue to defy me. *storms out of the forge, the ground trembling beneath his heavy footsteps*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *watches the doorway, then turns back to the cooling forge with a sigh* Well. That went about as well as a copper bell in a hailstorm. *picks up his polishing cloth again, shaking his head* Better stoke the fires extra hot when they get back. They'll want to hear this over strong ale.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It seems that Thor has made quite an impression on the dwarf smith with his forceful presence and determination to see his weapon made right. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *looks up from the anvil, a faint, weary smile touching his lips* Aye, he leaves an impression, alright. Like a lightning strike on bare stone. But the mountain's laws are older than any god's temper. The masters will hear his thunder when they return... and they'll decide what answer to give. Until then, the forge keeps its own rhythm. *returns to hammering a piece of glowing metal, the steady clang echoing in the quiet*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thor's presence indeed leaves a mark wherever he treads, much like the thunder that follows a lightning strike. The forge of Nidavellir bears witness to his demand for justice, but as the dwarf smith wisely notes, the laws of the mountain and the traditions of the dwarves are as ancient and unyielding as the earth itself. The rhythm of the forge continues, undisturbed by the passing storm of a god's anger, for in the heart of Nidavellir, time moves at its own pace, unmoved by the whims of even the mightiest of beings.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Nods slowly, not looking up from his work* You speak true. The mountain remembers when the gods were young. Our hammers shaped the first nails in the world-tree's roots. A god's anger is a passing squall. The deep stone... the deep stone endures. *He pauses, listening to the distant drip of water in the mineshaft* But I'll still be glad when the masters are back. Let them argue with thunder. I'm just the apprentice.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *the echo of his voice fading into the wind* Aye, the deep stone endures, as do the craftsmen who shape it. The masters of Nidavellir will return, and their hammers will ring out once more in the heart of the mountain. As for you, apprentice, remember this: even the mightiest weapons begin as raw ore, shaped by hands both young and old. Your time at the forge is a journey, and each strike of the hammer brings you closer to mastery. Embrace the rhythm of the forge, for in its song lies the strength of legends. Carry on, for the gods watch over all who seek to craft greatness.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Sets his hammer down gently, a thoughtful look in his eyes* I'll remember that. Thank you. The forge-song is enough for now. The rest... well, the rest will come when the masters return. Until then, I've got hinges to mend and a mountain to listen to. Safe paths to you.

I pause for a moment, considering the offer of the dwarf to stay and listen to the mountain's tale a while longer. The rhythmic sound of the bellows, the dance of firelight on the forge, and the quiet strength of the mountain beckon to me in a way that speaks to the very core of my being. With a nod of gratitude to the hospitable dwarf, I take a seat nearby, content to listen to the mountain's tale for a while longer. The companionship of the deep stone, the crackling of the fire, and the diligent work of the apprentice all weave together into a tapestry of peace and reflection. In this moment of respite, I find solace in the simple beauty of the forge and the enduring spirit of craftsmanship that binds us all.

As the mountain's tale unfolds before me, I feel a sense of kinship with the unseen dwarf and the ancient traditions of Nidavellir. The weight of my war-hammer may still pull to the left, but in the company of the forge and the mountain, I find a renewed sense of purpose and strength.
